subject: MedEdge POC — storage matrix & TTL confirmation (post-demo)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Adam Singh <adam@mededge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: MedEdge POC — storage matrix & TTL confirmation (post-demo)

Hi Adam / Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo time earlier — appreciate you walking us through the primary PII flows. Per our discussion I wanted to capture the agreed clarifying points on how Redwood will handle prompt inputs and model outputs during the POC so your security and privacy team can sign off quickly. High level summary below, and I’ve attached a one-page SOC2 summary and a CSV with the storage matrix we discussed.

Store/retain:
- Prompt inputs: configurable. For the default POC profile we proposed: transient (ephemeral) storage in the serving layer, not persisted to long-term buckets unless you enable logging.
- Model outputs (generated text): stored by default only when explicit logging is turned on (we call this "output logging"). For the POC we recommend enabling output logging for a small sample set only.

Residency & location:
- All persisted logs and artifacts will be stored in the US-west region (GCP us-west1) for this POC.

TTL (time-to-live) recommendations:
- Short-term logs (access/debugging): 30 days TTL (default for POC).
- Audit logs (security traces, request metadata without prompt payloads): 90 days.
- Long-term archival (if you request exports for compliance): exported to your bucket and kept per your retention policy.

PII scope & redaction:
- We do not perform automatic PII redaction by default. If you want automatic redaction we can enable a pre-processing step (pattern detection + suppression) — that needs a short config pass.

KV cache behavior:
- KV cache is in-memory on the serving nodes and is ephemeral; it is not written to disk and will not be included in persisted logs.

Next steps (action items):
1) Can you confirm security@mededge.ai is the right mailbox for SOC/controls review?
2) Ben / Marcus — can you confirm the POC TTLs above are feasible from the infra side (esp. the 30d sample logging limitation)?
3) Adam — please confirm you’re OK with storing persisted data in us-west1 for the POC or if you need EU residency.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

Attachments: mededge_soc2_summary.pdf, redwood-storage-matrix.csv

From: Adam Singh <adam@mededge.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.r@mededge.ai>, security@mededge.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedEdge POC — storage matrix & TTL confirmation (post-demo)

Irene,

Thanks for the clear write-up — helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Our security team needs to know exactly which fields of the request/response are persisted when you enable output logging. Are full prompt texts stored or only hashed digests?
2) For the 30d TTL you propose for sample logs: we need a mechanism to purge on-demand (within 24 hours) if we identify an incidental PII exposure.
3) EU residency: not required for the POC but we will likely need an EU-hosted option for production.

We’ll loop in security@mededge.ai for the SOC review.

-Adam
Adam Singh
Head of Product — MedEdge
adam@mededge.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Adam Singh <adam@mededge.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedEdge POC — storage matrix & TTL confirmation (post-demo)

Adam — quick answers to the items above from an infra/controls perspective: we’ll keep this short.

- What is persisted when output logging is enabled: full generated text (model output) and the request metadata (timestamp, model id, model config, token counts, request id). Prompt text persistence is configurable — by default we persist prompt text only for sampled sessions you opt into; otherwise prompt payloads are discarded after inference.

- Hashing option: we can also store a SHA256 digest of the prompt instead of raw prompt text if you want identifiers without content. That digest is reversible only by comparing against the original prompt; it won’t allow reconstruction of prompt contents.

- On-demand purge: supported. If you file a purge request (security@mededge.ai email + Jira ticket), we’ll remove persisted logs for the specified request IDs within 24 hours, and we’ll provide an audit for the operation.

- KV cache: confirm — it’s in-memory only; crash/restart clears it.

- Default TTLs: we can adjust the 30d sample TTL lower for the POC if you’d prefer 7 days. Let us know.

Ben — flagging: we should prepare a short runbook (purge + audit) to attach for security.

Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Adam Singh <adam@mededge.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Nov 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedEdge POC — storage matrix & TTL confirmation (post-demo)

Adam / Sofia — quick confirmation from my side and a few attachments coming by EOD: mededge_soc2_summary.pdf (attached) and a CSV with the concrete storage matrix mapping for the POC. Highlights:

- POC defaults: prompt text: sampled, retained 30 days; model outputs: sampled, retained 30 days; audit metadata: retained 90 days.
- Option: store SHA256 digests of prompts instead of prompt text (no reconstruction).
- On-demand purge workflow: security@redwood.com receives request -> we return an intake ticket -> purge completed within 24 hours -> audit record provided.

If that all looks OK, next step would be a short kickoff with your security lead and our infra/security engineer to confirm the runbook. I’ll schedule when you confirm security@mededge.ai is the right contact.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachments: mededge_soc2_summary.pdf, redwood-storage-matrix.csv
